theorems.name: Subgroup Test
theorems.statement: A non-empty subset H \subseteq G is a subgroup iff a*b^{-1} \in H for all a,b \in H.
theorems.intuition: This one condition automatically forces both closure and the presence of inverses.
theorems.proofSketch: Take a=b to get the identity; take a=e to get inverses; then general closure follows.
theorems.example: H={0,2,4} in Z_6 passes the test since differences of elements stay in H.
theorems.examReady: Check a*b^{-1} \in H for arbitrary a,b \in H in one pass.

theorems.name: Lagrange's Theorem
theorems.statement: If G is finite and H \le G, then |H| divides |G|; specifically |G|=[G:H]\cdot|H|.
theorems.intuition: Cosets of H partition G into equal-sized blocks; counting blocks gives the formula.
theorems.proofSketch: Show |aH|=|H| via a bijection h\mapsto ah; show distinct cosets are disjoint; sum block sizes.
theorems.example: A subgroup of S3 (order 6) must have order 1, 2, 3, or 6.
theorems.examReady: State the formula, note the converse is FALSE in general (cite A4).
